SNACK HACK: Frozen Sour Grapes 🙂‍↕️🤏🏼 Recipe ↓ Ingredients: * Green grapes * Sprite or your favorite juice * Fresh lime juice * Strawberry Jell-O powder Instructions: 1. Wash and dry the green grapes, then poke small holes in each grape with a toothpick. 2. Place the grapes in a bowl and pour in enough Sprite or juice to fully cover them. 3. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let the grapes soak up the flavor. 4. Drain the grapes, then toss them with fresh lime juice. 5. Sprinkle with strawberry Jell-O powder and toss until evenly coated. 6. Spread the grapes on a parchment-lined tray and freeze until completely frozen. 7. Enjoy straight from the freezer! #easyrecipes #5hourambassador #asmr

Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO) appeared to confuse the Atlanta Hawks NBA team and the University of Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball team as he sought to link former special counsel Jack Smith to Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis, who also brought charges against President Trump. The Missouri Republican asked whether Mr. Smith recalled attending a Hawks game against the Golden State Warriors in Atlanta in 2024, confusing Mr. Smith, who said he had no recollection of visiting Atlanta during that time. "I really don't think so. It's possible I flew through the Atlanta airport on the way to Florida, but I do not have a recollection of going to Atlanta. I definitely did not go to a Hawks game. I'm sure of that," he said. Sen. Schmitt said he had text messages showing that Mr. Smith had attended a "Hawks" game, which the senator suggested took place in Atlanta the day after Ms. Willis acknowledged having a personal relationship with Nathan Wade, the outside prosecutor she hired to work on her election interference case against President Trump. His staff briefly put up a poster with the alleged text messages before quickly taking it down without giving Mr. Smith the opportunity to read them. "You may think you're a hero in this story, but let me tell you something, you're the villain," Sen. Schmitt said as he concluded his questioning. "You have weaponized the Department of Justice against political enemies to an extent that has never happened in the history of this country. You will go down as a total dirtbag." Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) then pointed out that Sen. Schmitt appeared to have confused the Hawks with the Hawkeyes. "That might be the confusion over the names of the team. But perhaps you should have looked at it more carefully," she said, also criticizing Sen. Schmitt for calling Mr. Smith a "dirtbag." Mr. Smith confirmed he attended the Iowa Hawkeyes game at the University of Maryland on Feb. 3, 2024, to see Caitlin Clark play. #caitlinclark #iowahawkeyes #jacksmith #cspan

Crispy cheeseburger wraps Ingredients  For the beef mixture: 1 lb ground beef ( 80% lean, 20% fat ) 2 tbsp oil 1 yellow onion, finely diced  1 tbsp fresh garlic, minced 1 tbsp tomato paste Salt to taste 1 tsp black pepper  1 tbsp garlic powder  2 tsp smoked paprika powder  1 tsp onion powder  1 large jalapeño, chopped 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce  1/2 cup water For the cheese burger sauce: 1/2 cup mayonnaise 2 tbsp ketchup 1 tbsp yellow mustard 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce  1 1/2 tbsp finely minced dill pickles 1 tbsp pickle juice 1 tsp finely minced onion 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/4 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp sugar 1/4 tsp black pepper To assemble: 9 medium tortilla wraps 1 1/2 cup Mexican style four cheese  1/2 cup caramelized onions 1/3 cup picked jalapeños, chopped  Oil for pan frying  Method: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook 3–4 minutes until softened. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and fully cooked. Drain excess fat if needed, leaving a little behind. Add tomato paste, salt, pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika and onion powder. Cook 1–2 minutes. Add Worcestershire sauce jalapeños and water. Simmer uncovered 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has completely reduced and the beef is moist but not watery. Taste and adjust salt if needed. Remove from heat and cool slightly. For the sauce, mix mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, pickles, pickle juice, onion, garlic powder, smoked paprika, sugar and black pepper until smooth. Refrigerate until ready to use. Lay out the tortillas and spread about 1 tbsp sauce slightly below the center. Add about 1/4 cup beef, 2 tbsp cheese, caramelized onions and pickled jalapeños. Fold the bottom over the filling, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat. Place wraps seam-side down and cook 2–3 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and crispy. Continue cooking until all sides are crisp and the cheese is melted. Rest 1–2 minutes, slice in half and serve immediately with extra cheeseburger sauce.  #recipe #cheeseburger
